newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss watch exports rise in five months to May.
newsitem.headline: Swiss watch exports rise in five months to May.

text.p: Exports of Swiss watches hit a record high in value terms in the first five months of 1997, with watches and watch part exports rising 5.6 percent to 3.1 billion Swiss francs ($2.2 billion), said Francois Habersaat, president of the Swiss Watch Industry (FH).

In the text of an address to be presented to the industry's annual meeting, he said the value of exported watches excluding parts totaled at 2.8 billion francs. This was 8.2 percent higher than in the same period of the previous year.
In volume terms however, exports fell 13.4 percent in the five-month period, he said.
Exports of plastic watches were down significantly in the 1997 period while steel watch exports rose. Exports of gold watches increased by one percent.
Exports to Hong Kong rose 4.1 percent, those to the U.S. rose 15.6 percent, and exports to Germany rose 8.2 percent.

In May alone, total exports were up 8.8 percent from the comparable period a year earlier. The industry reported last year that exports of watches and movements from January to May 1996 totalled 2.98 billion Swiss francs in value.
